messages:
Maya (CS): Quick check-in on Acme onboarding. They completed SDK integration but are seeing 350-600ms p95 on small chat turns. Renewal in 6 weeks, flagged as medium risk if latency doesn't improve. Looking for a compact, customer-facing safety-net we can hand to their engineers today (prefetch + batch + streaming guidance).
Ravi (Solutions): TL;DR we should recommend: 1) warmup calls for top intents, 2) short prefix prefetch, 3) conservative batching window for interactive flows, 4) enable streaming where UX supports it. I can draft a 10-line runbook.
Jordan (SRE): Agree. For production SLOs we prefer: p95 <= 250ms for quick-turn flows. Ops notes: set routing policy to prefer cached model variant and keep an autoscale buffer. Also watch KV cache hit ratio.
Maya (CS): Can you paste the 10-line runbook here? We want something our CSMs can send to customers without ops edits. Keep it actionable.
Ravi (Solutions): Here — copy/paste for customer: ```Runbook: 1) Identify top 20 intents/utterances via logs. 2) Deploy a warmup job: call model with those prefixes every 60s for first 30m after deploy. 3) Configure prefix prefetch (store KV snapshots for those prefixes). 4) Set batching window to 5–20ms for interactive routes; 50ms for async routes. 5) Enable streaming responses so UI can show partial tokens while batch completes. 6) If p95 > 300ms, rollback to cached model variant and open ticket.```
Ava (Acme): Thanks — trying the warmup. One question: how intrusive is the warmup traffic for our bill? We have tight budget on infra.
Ravi (Solutions): Warmup cost is small if you limit to top intents and tune frequency. Example: 20 intents * 1 call/min * 60min = 1,200 calls. If each call ~20 tokens, it's negligible vs regular volume. We can also set warmup to hit a cheaper quantized model variant.
Jordan (SRE): Ops tip: use short-lived prefetch TTLs (2–5m) during high churn onboarding, longer (10–30m) once steady. Also add a fallback route in routing policy: if cache miss and queue depth > threshold, route to cheaper quantized model with graceful degradation.
Maya (CS): Adding a tiny checklist for the CSM to track account health: - Onboarding progress: SDK done? (yes) - Warmup enabled? (Ava to confirm) - p95 baseline before/after warmup - Billing impact estimate sent - Renewal risk flag updated in CRM
Ava (Acme): Warmup enabled (rolling out now), set TTL to 3m. Seeing slight improvement in first 10 minutes. Will share p95 in ~30m.
deploy-bot: deploy-redwood/qa -> prod: rolling update started for model-routing v2 at 1834567905.
Jordan (SRE): FYI the routing update will add the fallback policy I mentioned. Monitor queue_depth and cached_kv_hit metrics.
Ravi (Solutions): If you need a one-click snippet for their engineers to paste, use this curl example: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.sh/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -d '{"model":"cached-claude-lite","prompt":"<intent prefix>","stream":true}'
```
Maya (CS): Great. Ava — once you have p95 numbers, I'll update the renewal risk and propose a small discount if needed (to keep them engaged while we stabilize). Also capturing their feedback: the team mentioned difficulty with streaming SDK examples — I'll loop in DevEx for a sample.
Ava (Acme): p95 down to ~220ms after 45m. Looks promising. The streaming sample would help for our frontend.
Maya (CS): Perfect — I'll mark onboarding as green-probationary and drop a note in CRM. Follow-up items: DevEx sample, confirm cost delta, final renewal suggestion. :white_check_mark:
